articles.title: Space telescope Euclid sets the new standard for cosmology
articles.description: On July 1, 2023, the European Space Agency (ESA) launched the Euclid space telescope into space. Its mission: to create the largest and most detailed map of the universe ever made.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope, launched in July 2023, is revolutionizing cosmology by mapping the universe's structure and dark matter distribution. This mission marks a new standard for understanding the cosmos.

articles.title: Euclid offers best-ever 3D map of the universe to date
articles.description: The Euclid Consortium and the European Space Agency (ESA) have released the first major batch of data from the Euclid space telescope. This release, which captures light from more than a billion objects and covers an area of sky equivalent to 9,500 full moons, lays the foundation for Europe's dark universe detective's largest-ever 3D map of the cosmos. Several German research facilities play crucial roles in the Euclid mission's success.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The Euclid Consortium and ESA have released the first major data release featuring the best-ever 3D map of the universe to date. This landmark achievement provides unprecedented insights into cosmic structure and dark matter.

articles.title: A massive new simulation reveals how the universe emerged from darkness
articles.description: A groundbreaking new supercomputer simulation is revealing how the universe escaped its cosmic dark age and transformed into a cosmos filled with stars and galaxies. Called Lumina, it recreates 2 billion years of early cosmic history across a region 1.6 billion light-years wide, capturing extraordinary details that previous simulations could not.
articles.summary: A groundbreaking supercomputer simulation reveals how the universe transitioned from its cosmic dark age into the luminous universe we observe today. This achievement provides revolutionary insights into cosmic history and structure formation.

articles.title: NASA reveals bold new plan to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028
articles.description: NASA has revealed an accelerated plan to land astronauts on the Moon in 2028, with SpaceX and Blue Origin developing competing lunar landers and a crucial orbital test scheduled for 2027. Faster rocket preparations, new lightweight spacesuits, and redesigned missions could help pave the way for a permanent lunar presence and future human exploration of Mars.
articles.summary: NASA has announced an accelerated timeline to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028, with SpaceX and Blue Origin developing lunar landers. This bold initiative marks a major milestone in human space exploration and lunar return missions.

articles.title: Caltech robot makes history by building a structure in space
articles.description: For the first time, a robot has autonomously built part of a structure in space, demonstrating a breakthrough that could fundamentally change space exploration. The technology could one day allow scientists to construct enormous telescopes, communications antennas, and solar power stations in orbit, far beyond the size limits of today's rockets.
articles.summary: A Caltech robot has achieved a historic first by autonomously constructing part of a structure in space, opening new possibilities for future construction and assembly in the cosmos.

articles.title: SpaceX's Starship megarocket will launch to orbit on Nov. 13. Will you be able to spot it in the night sky?
articles.description: "It should be very bright, considerably brighter than the Starlink satellites due to its size."
articles.summary: SpaceX's Starship megarocket is set to launch to orbit, and observers may be able to witness the exceptionally bright spacecraft in the night sky.

articles.title: NASA’s Hubble Offers Cosmic Sampler of Targets for Roman
articles.description: A gallery of gravitational lenses captured by NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope showcases the diversity of this cosmic phenomenon and lays the groundwork for follow-up observations by the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.
articles.summary: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope provides a diverse gallery of gravitational lens images, demonstrating this cosmic phenomenon's potential for the Roman Space Telescope's future observations.

articles.title: Euclid's First Data Release: A Stepping Stone to its 3D Map of the Sky
articles.description: The ESA's Euclid Space Telescope has released its first huge batch of data. It's all part of the telescope's mission to study dark energy and dark matter. The telescope is busy creating the largest ever 3D map of the Universe with its huge 600 megapixel camera, and new images give us some highlights.
articles.summary: The ESA's Euclid Space Telescope releases its first major data batch, advancing humanity's goal to create a comprehensive 3D map of the universe.

articles.title: Asteroid Bennu's Sample Delivers Another Surprise
articles.description: Researchers compared the samples from asteroid Bennu with the Murchison meteorite and measured the amino acid β-alanine in both. Using new techniques, they were able to measure not only their isotopic compositions, but isotopic differences between individual atoms in the same molecule. The results show that some of the same pre-cursors to life formed in different conditions and positions in the protoplanetary disk.
articles.summary: Analysis of samples from asteroid Bennu reveals the presence of amino acids, providing compelling evidence for organic chemistry in the early solar system.

articles.title: The Chandra X-Ray Observatory Unmasks a Supernova Impostor
articles.description: Some stars, called Luminous Blue Variables, can be confused with supernovae explosions. They exhibit similar outbursts, but unlike supernovae, which explode once and then are gone forever, these stars have periodic outbursts. New research found that one of these 'supernova impostors' is in a binary relationship with a black hole or a neutron star, and that explains its periodic outbursts.
articles.summary: NASA's Chandra X-Ray Observatory helps distinguish between Luminous Blue Variables and supernovae by analyzing their distinct outburst characteristics. This advancement improves astronomers' ability to accurately classify stellar phenomena.

articles.title: Hubble offers cosmic sampler of targets for Roman
articles.description: A gallery of gravitational lenses captured by NASA's Hubble Space Telescope showcases the diversity of this cosmic phenomenon and lays the groundwork for follow-up observations by the new Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The Hubble Space Telescope has captured a diverse collection of gravitational lenses that will serve as targets for NASA's upcoming Roman Space Telescope. These observations demonstrate the rich variety of gravitational lensing phenomena across the cosmos.

articles.title: Space dust particles point to ancient heavy-oxygen water reservoir in the Kuiper belt
articles.description: Way out past the asteroid belt, another belt encircles the planets in our solar system. The Kuiper belt, beyond Neptune, preserves icy bodies that escaped much of the processing experienced by objects closer to the sun. Unlike the rocky and metallic asteroid belt, Kuiper belt objects are composed mostly of frozen water, methane and ammonia, mixed with rock and dust.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Analysis of space dust particles reveals evidence of an ancient water reservoir containing heavy oxygen in the Kuiper Belt. This discovery provides insights into the early solar system's composition and water distribution.

articles.title: A rare star system emits radio signals every 8 minutes
articles.description: Scientists at the Curtin University node at the International Center for Radio Astronomy Research (ICRAR) have linked mysterious radio pulses to an unusual pairing of stars—a dead star that spins every eight minutes and a star similar to our own sun.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Researchers have identified a rare star system emitting mysterious radio signals at precise 8-minute intervals. This discovery opens new avenues for understanding exotic stellar objects and radio astronomy phenomena.

articles.title: A new view of the gamma-ray gap: 14 years of Fermi data reveal around 450 sources in a largely unexplored energy range
articles.description: The universe is filled with light at many different energies. Some of it is invisible to our eyes, including extremely energetic gamma rays, which can only be produced in the most extreme environments in our universe, for example supermassive black holes, exploding stars or astrophysical jets. To "see" gamma rays, astrophysicists use particle experiments in space, such as the Fermi-Large Area Telescope (Fermi-LAT). This instrument was launched into space by NASA in 2008, and it can detect photons from 20 megaelectronvolts (MeV, a unit of energy) to beyond 1 teraelectronvolt (TeV).
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Fourteen years of data from NASA's Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope have revealed approximately 450 previously unexplored sources in the gamma-ray energy range. This breakthrough expands our understanding of high-energy cosmic phenomena.

articles.title: Simulated collisions reveal how Phobos could preserve rocks blasted off Mars
articles.description: Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos, but their origins remain uncertain. Were they asteroids captured by Mars' gravity, or did they form from debris following a giant impact on the planet?
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Advanced simulations reveal how Mars' moon Phobos could capture and preserve rocks blasted from the Martian surface. This research illuminates the complex dynamics of planetary moons and ancient solar system history.

articles.title: Earth's fiery birth may have created hundreds of oceans' worth of water
articles.description: Earth's water may have been born in the planet's fiery atmosphere rather than delivered by icy comets or asteroids. Scientists discovered that rocky pebbles reacting with hydrogen under extreme heat can produce water in minutes, potentially generating hundreds of oceans' worth during Earth's formation. The findings suggest that water may be a natural part of how rocky planets form, rather than something that must arrive from space.
articles.summary: New research suggests Earth's water originated in our planet's fiery early atmosphere rather than being delivered by comets or asteroids. This discovery revolutionizes our understanding of Earth's habitability and water's origins.

articles.title: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe discovers a hidden pattern in the Sun’s chaotic magnetic fields
articles.description: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe has revealed a surprising secret hidden within the chaos of space: turbulent magnetic fields reverse their direction of rotation when examined at extremely small scales. The discovery exposes an unexpected pattern in solar wind turbulence that could help scientists better understand solar activity and predict geomagnetic storms.
articles.summary: NASA's Parker Solar Probe has uncovered hidden patterns within the Sun's turbulent magnetic fields, revealing previously unknown solar dynamics. This discovery enhances our understanding of solar physics and space weather.

articles.title: A radical theory says the universe is twice as old as we thought
articles.description: A provocative new cosmological model suggests the Universe could be 26.7 billion years old and might not need dark matter or dark energy to explain its behavior. University of Ottawa researchers tested the theory against several major astronomical observations, finding that it could explain galaxy rotation, cosmic expansion, and the formation of early elements.
articles.summary: A new cosmological model proposes the Universe could be 26.7 billion years old and challenges our understanding of dark matter and cosmic age.

articles.title: This supernova impostor baffled astronomers for 15 years — until they found a hidden black hole feeding on an unstable star
articles.description: A hidden black hole or neutron star companion to an unstable massive star is causing the system to erupt in light that mimics a supernova explosion.
articles.summary: Astronomers solved a 15-year mystery by discovering a hidden black hole or neutron star causing dramatic eruptions in an unstable star system.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 12, 2014: European Philae probe lands on Comet 67P, bounced twice and then got lost for nearly 2 years
articles.description: On Nov. 12, 2014, a European spacecraft named Philae landed on Comet 67P, then bounced twice and got lost. Here's why it mattered.
articles.summary: The European Philae probe made history on November 12, 2014, by landing on Comet 67P in a daring mission that demonstrated humanity's ability to explore distant cosmic objects.

articles.title: Dark matter breakthrough coming? Euclid space telescope unveils its 1st look into the dark universe (video)
articles.description: The Euclid space telescope released its first major batch of data, capturing the light of more than a billion objects over an area of sky as big as 9,500 full moons.
articles.summary: The Euclid space telescope released groundbreaking data capturing light from over a billion objects to advance our understanding of dark matter and the universe's structure.

articles.title: Pakistani astronaut set to become 1st international visitor to China's Tiangong space station this month
articles.description: China will fly its first foreign astronaut on the Shenzhou 24 mission, with a Pakistani pilot set for a roughly week-long stay aboard the Tiangong space station.
articles.summary: A Pakistani astronaut is set to become the first international visitor to China's Tiangong space station, marking a significant milestone in international space cooperation.

articles.title: NASA opens applications for astronauts who will live on the Moon
articles.description: If you ever wanted to earn a solid wage by living and working on another world, now's your chance. NASA has put out a call for a new generation of ast...
articles.summary: NASA is now accepting applications for astronauts who will live and work on the Moon, opening an extraordinary opportunity for future lunar explorers.

articles.title: Physicists step closer to the 'Zeptoverse' after 42-year particle search
articles.description: Physicists have found evidence of a particle decay so rare that it is expected to occur only around once in every 10 billion "beauty" particles. The result, from the upgraded LHCb experiment at CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC), follows a search spanning mor…
articles.summary: Physicists have discovered evidence of an extraordinarily rare particle decay after a 42-year search, occurring approximately once in every 10 billion interactions. This breakthrough advances fundamental understanding of particle physics and exotic matter.

articles.title: Step inside the zeptoverse: British scientists use the Large Hadron Collider to peer inside a minuscule world where exotic particles may be hiding
articles.description: British scientists have used the Large Hadron Collider to peer inside the minuscule world of the zeptoverse.
articles.summary: British scientists used the Large Hadron Collider to explore the zeptoverse, a minuscule realm where exotic particles may exist. This research opens new frontiers in understanding the fundamental structure of matter.

articles.title: NASA takes an all-hands-on-deck approach in its return to the Moon
articles.description: Senior NASA officials held a lengthy news conference last weekend, laying out a series of lunar contract awards, new contract opportunities, and mission decisions. They followed one after the other: landers, nuclear-powered rovers, scouting drones, power gene…
articles.summary: NASA announced a comprehensive strategy for lunar return missions, revealing new contract awards and ambitious plans for Moon exploration. This coordinated effort marks a pivotal moment in humanity's return to the lunar surface.

articles.title: 378 dias sem janelas: NASA termina mais uma experiência para preparar viagens a Marte
articles.description: A NASA concluiu recentemente a segunda missão CHAPEA, onde quatro voluntários passaram 378 dias num habitat simulado de Marte, construído por impressão 3D e sem janelas. O objetivo é preparar a futura exploração humana do planeta vermelho. Um ano de isolament…
articles.summary: NASA completed its second CHAPEA mission, where four volunteers spent 378 days in a simulated Mars habitat to advance human Mars exploration readiness. This groundbreaking experiment brings crewed Mars missions closer to reality.

articles.title: Für Solaranlagen oder Teleskopspiegel: Roboter baut autonom Strukturen im All
articles.description: Im Rahmen des von der US-Forschungsagentur Darpa finanzierten Nom4d-Projekts hat ein Caltech-Roboter erstmals autonom eine Struktur im All errichtet. Das soll künftig den Bau großer Solaranlagen oder Teleskopspiegel erleichtern.weiterlesen auf t3n.de
articles.summary: A Caltech-developed robot, funded by DARPA, autonomously constructed structures in space for the first time as part of the Nom4d project. This achievement represents a major milestone toward robotic space construction for solar arrays and telescopes.

articles.title: PROMISE: Der neue NASA-Mondrover PROMISE
articles.description: Die NASA plant eine revolutionäre Rückkehr zum Mond: Ein neuer Rover und innovative Missionen bereiten den Weg für Menschen.
articles.summary: NASA is developing the revolutionary PROMISE lunar rover as part of an ambitious Moon return strategy with innovative missions ahead. This advanced rover represents a transformative step toward human lunar exploration and colonization.

articles.title: I Am Artemis Katie Spicer
articles.description: For Katie Spicer, embracing opportunity and challenge has led to giant leaps during her time at NASA. Now as the NASA lander integration lead for Blue Origin’s Blue Moon Mark 2 lander, one of the commercially provided human landing systems for NASA’s Artemis program, Spicer will have her handprint on history. Spicer works in the […]
articles.summary: Katie Spicer's career at NASA demonstrates how embracing challenges leads to significant achievements in space exploration and scientific advancement.
